args.complete_required_delivery_text:
Controlled dribbling and court awareness

The UGA chapter emphasizes fingertip control rather than the palm and describes dribbling with one hand at a time. Keeping the head raised is presented as a way to notice defenders, teammates and surrounding space. The chapter also advises limiting unnecessary dribbling because a pass can move the ball forward quickly and create openings. Direction changes may involve a crossover, a behind-the-back movement or a transfer between the legs. Its central control concept is being able to handle the ball on either side and transfer it between hands while maintaining awareness.

General introductory basketball reference, selected and paraphrased from the cited chapter. No youth-specific suitability, training dose, medical clearance or planner approval is established.

Source: 3. Fundamentals – Dribbling, Ch.1 - Basketball, UGA PEDB Program. https://open.online.uga.edu/basketball/chapter/fundamentals-dribbling/
